market_context: U.S. equities are rebounding sharply from last week's AI-led selloff as oil declines on hopes of easing Iran-war tensions, while volatility has fallen materially. (apnews.com) The rebound is late-day extended ahead of Tuesday's October CPI report, while Nvidia remains an idiosyncratic drag amid its board investigation concerning CEO Jensen Huang. (ca.investing.com)

predictions.reasoning: SPY is only about 0.1% beneath its intraday high after a 2.61% advance, leaving limited room for further upside into the closing auction. The broad rally is largely a recovery from last week's risk-off move, while CPI risk remains immediately ahead on Tuesday. ([apnews.com)

QQQ has gained 3.76% and is close to its session high, a sharp rebound following the recent AI-sector rout. The index remains vulnerable to late profit-taking because the market's central AI bellwether, Nvidia, is still down roughly 5% on a CEO-related investigation. (apnews.com)

Nvidia's board investigation into reports that Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort is an unresolved company-specific risk, not a catalyst that has been cleared during the session. The stock remains notably weak despite the broad technology rebound, indicating persistent selling and rotation away from Nvidia exposure. (apnews.com)

Tesla is up 6.47% and trading just below its intraday high, making it susceptible to closing-auction profit-taking after an outsized rebound. The session's risk-on move has been broad, but CPI uncertainty for Tuesday and a still-elevated 10-year yield argue against extending the late-day momentum materially. (apnews.com)
